memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him for three months. But when she could hide him no longer, she got a papyrus basket for him and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in it and put it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile." - Exodus 2:2b-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three months of hiding a baby in a house, hushing every cry, listening for footsteps outside. Then the terrible day when hiding is no longer possible.

So she makes a basket. She waterproofs it carefully with tar and pitch — the same Hebrew word used for Noah's ark. And she places her son in the very river that was meant to swallow him.

This was not a mother giving up. Hebrews tells us plainly that Moses' parents acted by faith and were not afraid of the king's edict (Heb 11:23). Faith here looks like doing the most careful, practical thing you can — and then letting go.

There comes a point in every parent's life, and in every believer's life, when we have done all we can and must place someone we love into God's hands. It feels like release into danger. It is actually release into God's keeping.

The little ark floated on the water because the God who once kept Noah was keeping this child too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What or whom am I holding tightly because I am afraid to trust God with them?
2. Have I done what I can, and now need to let God do what only He can?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I place into Your hands what I cannot protect. Give me a mother's courage — to do my best and then to trust You fully. Amen.
